1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen, the last module. You know the material. This module is about turning it into points on the day: time, reading questions, scenarios, multi-select, traps, the final week, exam day and what follows. It uses only what I A P P publishes, and makes no predictions about the questions.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Plan your time across the two halves. Read a stem and a scenario in a fixed order: the ask, the role, the instrument and the stage. Answer multi-select questions with exactly the right number of options. Match your answer to the depth the verb asks for. Eliminate options that fall into the common traps. And prepare the final week and exam day.

1.title: The Exam in One Page
1.text: The exam in one page. One hundred items, all multiple choice, including case studies and scenarios; no essays; one point for each correct answer. Two and three-quarter hours of testing time, with a fifteen-minute break halfway. The break divides the exam into two halves, each with half the questions and half the time, and the first half cannot be reopened after you submit it. The passing score is three hundred on a scale of one hundred to five hundred, and section percentages cannot be averaged to find it. Questions come from the Body of Knowledge, but you may need to apply it to new situations. As of the twenty-seventh of October, twenty twenty-six, confirm the format on I A P P's pages.

1.title: Pacing: About Ninety-Nine Seconds a Question
1.text: Start with arithmetic. One hundred sixty-five minutes for one hundred items is about ninety-nine seconds an item. Each half has fifty questions in eighty-two and a half minutes. Use checkpoints: question twenty-five by about forty-one minutes, question fifty by about eighty-two minutes, and then the same again in the second half. Bank time: short definition questions take less, scenarios take more. Cap a hard question: choose your best answer, flag it and move on. And use the break to reset, not to study. Exam tip: a hard question is worth the same single point as an easy one.

1.title: Reading a Stem: Five Steps
1.text: Read every stem in five steps. One: find the ask, in the last sentence. Words such as best, first and most likely change the answer. Two: read the facts: who is involved, which system, where and when. Three: mark the role, the instrument and the stage. Four: predict an answer before you read the options. Five: match and eliminate; the options are written to tempt, so compare each with your prediction. And skip nothing: a number, a region or a date in the stem is there for a reason. Exam tip: predict first.

1.title: Scenario Questions: Role, Instrument and Stage
1.text: A scenario is a bundle of facts. Sort them into three lenses before you read the options. Role: who are we? Provider, deployer, controller, processor. The role decides whose duties apply. Instrument: which law, standard or framework governs? That decides which rule applies. Stage: where are we in the life cycle? That decides which control fits. The table shows the Helios example: Helios builds a chat on a Corvid Labs model and offers it under its own name, so it is the provider of the chat. Distractors often give a right answer for the wrong role, instrument or stage. Exam tip: do the sort every time.

1.title: Multi-Select: Exactly N, No Partial Credit
1.text: For multi-select, the stem says how many to select. Select exactly that number. There is no partial credit: one wrong choice, or one missing, scores nothing. Judge each option on its own as true or false for this stem, then count the trues. If you have more trues than the number asked for, re-read the stem for the qualifier: first, best, most. If you have fewer, re-check the options you marked false; one may be right in this context. And watch for options that are true in general but do not answer this stem. Exam tip: each option is its own true-or-false question.

1.title: The Verbs Set the Depth: How to Answer
1.text: Module zero said that the verb that starts an indicator sets the depth of the question. Here is how to use that. Understand and identify: the correct statement, or the term that fits. Apply, conduct and perform: the best action in the situation. Evaluate and assess: the best-justified judgment. Create and establish: the policy or control that must exist. If two options are both true, pick the one that fits the depth of the verb. The table adds how to choose between two true options. Exam tip: ask what the question wants you to do with the knowledge: recall it, choose with it, judge with it or build with it.

1.title: Eliminating Options: Traps That Look Right
1.text: Six traps make a wrong option look right. Absolute words: always, never, only and all are rarely true in governance. The wrong role: a provider duty handed to the deployer, or the reverse. The wrong stage: a monitoring fix for a design problem. The wrong instrument: a G D P R rule for an A I Act question. True but off-question: a correct fact that does not answer this stem. And the skipped step: going live before the assessment, or acting before containing the harm. Exam tip: strike the options that fail on role, instrument or stage; what is left is usually the answer.

1.title: Flagging, Changing Answers and the First-Half Rule
1.text: Use flags for questions you want to revisit within a half; the forward and backward arrows move between questions. The first half is final: after you submit it you cannot return, so clear your flags first. Answer every question, because each correct answer earns a point and a blank cannot. Change an answer only for a reason: a fact you recalled or a qualifier you missed, not a feeling. Keep a few minutes at the end of each half for flagged items. And do not carry doubt into the second half. Exam tip: finish and review the first half before you submit it.

1.title: Look-Alike Pairs the Course Teaches Apart
1.text: Some concepts look alike and are taught apart. D P I A and F R I A: personal data rights under the G D P R, against fundamental rights, for certain deployers, under the A I Act. Provider and deployer: who builds, and who uses. Controller and processor: who decides, and who acts on behalf. Red teaming, audit and threat modeling: try to break it, check compliance, and map attack paths. Incident, issue and risk: it happened and harmed, a problem was found, it may happen. Deactivate and localize: off, or limited. And N I S T, I S O and O E C D: framework, certifiable standard and principles. Exam tip: check the stem for which side applies.

2.title: Your Final Week: A Plan
2.text: A plan for the final week. I A P P recommends at least thirty hours of study in total, so the final week consolidates. Remember that study materials are tools, not a one-to-one guide to the exam. Days seven and six: sweep all four domains with the recap pages. Day five: practice one timed half, fifty questions in eighty-two and a half minutes. Day four: sort every miss by cause: role, instrument, stage, verb or a missed qualifier. Days three and two: weak domains, then the Dates and Verify live pages, the glossary and the pairs. Day one: light review, logistics and sleep. Exam tip: fix the cause of each miss.

2.title: Exam Day at a Test Center
2.text: At a test center, arrive fifteen minutes early; a late arrival may be treated as a no-show, and all fees are forfeited. Bring two qualifying forms of I D that meet the test center's requirements. No electronic devices and no reading material are allowed in the exam room. The timer does not stop if you leave the room for a break. You may reschedule or cancel up to forty-eight hours before the appointment, and you should wait for the confirmation email. Request special accommodations as early as you can. As of the twenty-seventh of October, twenty twenty-six, check the handbook before you book. Exam tip: make the logistics boring.

2.title: Exam Day Online With OnVUE
2.text: For online testing with OnVUE, use a personal computer, not a work-issued one, with no virtual private network, and run the system check on the microphone, webcam and internet speed. Check-in opens thirty minutes before. You photograph yourself, a government-issued I D and four views of your surroundings. The rules: keep your face in view, stay at your workspace, nobody else in the room, no headphones, one beverage only, and no speaking aloud. A human proctor watches by webcam and microphone; A I assists, and a person makes the decisions. You may change or cancel the appointment until fifteen minutes after the scheduled start. As of the twenty-seventh of October, twenty twenty-six, confirm the rules.

2.title: After the Exam: Results, Breakdown and Next Steps
2.text: Results are immediate: pass or fail, and the score. A later email gives a breakdown by section; I A P P does not give the number of correct answers. If you do not pass, you may retake no sooner than seven days after the attempt, at a discounted price, and the section breakdown shows where to aim your study. If you pass, certification maintenance is two hundred fifty dollars for a two-year term, or I A P P membership at two hundred ninety-five dollars a year, plus twenty credits a year. Exams are updated each year, about ten to fifteen percent of content, announced at least ninety days ahead. As of the twenty-seventh of October, twenty twenty-six, confirm fees and rules.

2.title: Final Checklist
2.text: A final checklist. Technique: ninety-nine seconds a question, checkpoints at twenty-five and fifty, find the ask, role, instrument and stage, predict then match, and exactly the right number for multi-select. Traps: absolutes, the wrong role, stage or instrument, true but off-question, and the skipped step. First half: flag, review and clear it before you submit. Review: the recap pages, glossary, look-alike pairs, and the Dates and Verify live pages. Logistics: I D, route or room, system check, confirmation email and sleep. And mindset: every question is one point; take the next one.

2.title: Case Set: The Helios Candidate Chat
2.text: Now a case set: one scenario, five questions. Helios plans a candidate chat. Job applicants in the E U and in New York City ask about roles and the hiring process, and can ask it to summarize their own résumé. It runs on the general-purpose model from Corvid Labs, used through an interface and grounded on Helios's careers pages. Anika Berg's team wants to launch in six weeks. Jonas Weber notes that the chat will process applicants' personal data. Mei Tanaka notes that it will accept free-text input from anyone. Samira Haddad asks the governance lead for a recommendation before the launch decision. Answer each question from the case, using role, instrument and stage.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. In the Helios candidate chat case, which describes Helios's role for the chat? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Helios builds the chat on the model and offers it under its own name, so it is the provider of the chat, and it also deploys the Corvid Labs model. A feature built on a model does not make Helios a mere distributor.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. In the Helios candidate chat case, which two checks should the governance lead make first? Select two. The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and E. Personal data brings the G D P R, and a system that interacts with people brings the A I Act's transparency duties under Article fifty. Medical device, vehicle and nuclear rules have nothing to do with a careers chat.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. The Helios team wants to launch the candidate chat in six weeks. Which activity belongs at the decision-to-deploy stage and should be finished before launch? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Before go-live the deployer assesses the system it chose, with the provider's documents and its own tests. Reading logs and answering a leak come after launch, and retirement comes at the end.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. During testing of the candidate chat, a tester types hidden instructions into the free-text box and the chat reveals part of its configuration. Which risk is this, and what is the best next step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Hidden instructions in input that change the system's behavior are prompt injection. Add controls on inputs, outputs and permissions, and retest with red teaming.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Weeks after launch, the candidate chat gives applicants visa-sponsorship details taken from an outdated careers page. What is the best response? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The cause is a stale document in the retrieval source, so contain the harm, record the incident, fix the document, retest and communicate. Waiting, retraining the whole model and deleting evidence make things worse.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are the five answers. Question one: A. Question two: A and E. Question three: C. Question four: A. Question five: D. That completes the course. You have covered all four domains, thirteen competencies and fifty-eight indicators, with a recap, a glossary and a method for the day. Use the recap pages, practice in timed halves, and fix the cause of every miss. Good luck with the exam.
